name: Cargo Power-Assisted Bicycle
description: A conventional-looking pedal bicycle on two or three wheels built to carry cargo, weighing more than 55 kg, with an electric motor of up to 1,000 W that stops assisting at 32 km/h, allowed on a municipality's roads only where its by-laws permit.

restrictions.rule: Allowed only under a provincial pilot project evaluating cargo e-bikes
A pedal-driven bicycle of conventional exposed fork-and-frame design with two or three wheels, pedals that are always operable, handlebar steering, and a platform, basket or container for cargo
Weighs more than 55 kg, and is no more than 1.3 m wide, 4 m long and 2.2 m high, with no structure fully enclosing the rider
An electric motor with a continuous rated output of 1,000 W or less that can't assist at 32 km/h or more, stopping when the throttle is released or the brakes are applied
Must not be modified to exceed 1,000 W or 32 km/h, or to add any other non-muscular propulsion
Riders must be 16 or older, and every rider and passenger must wear a bicycle or motorcycle helmet
Passengers only if it was manufactured to carry them; no dangerous goods, and loads must be secured
Needs a bell or horn, a white or amber front light, a red rear light or reflector, and reflective material front and rear
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's licence, registration, plates or insurance, though municipal by-laws on motorized vehicles apply unless they say otherwise
Allowed on a municipality's roads, sidewalks, trails, paths or parks only where its by-laws permit; on the road it must use a bike lane where there is one
Not allowed on the 400-series highways or the other controlled-access highways listed in Regulations 627 and 630
